_comment: Input spec for layout/digital/tap_distance.py -- the well/substrate
tap-DISTANCE check on the digital partition's routed GDS (issue #448).
This is deliberately a separate artifact from erc-supply-spec.json: that
spec asks 'does every well have a tie at all' (klt erc erc.missing_tie,
presence only). The rules here ask 'how far is every diffusion from its
nearest tie', which is a different, distance-valued question. Neither
result implies the other; reports/erc-supply.json keeps its narrower
meaning unchanged.
Rule source: GlobalFoundries GF180MCU Design Rule Manual (DRM), section
14.3 'Latch-up Rules and Guidelines', 14.3.1 'Core Latch-up Rules and
Guidelines', as published in the open PDK documentation at
https://gf180mcu-pdk.readthedocs.io/en/latest/physical_verification/design_manual/drm_14_3_1.html
(retrieved 2026-10-10). The installed open-PDK KLayout rule decks
(libs.tech/klayout/tech/drc/rule_decks, pinned variant gf180mcuD) do NOT
code any LU.* rule (their own comments reference latch-up only in
MDP/LDMOS notes), and klt's curated gf180mcu deck has no tie-distance
rule either (`klt deck rules --deck gf180mcu` lists none), so these
limits are transcribed from the DRM text, not read from an executable
deck. The DRM table has two voltage columns, LV (3.3 V devices) and MV
(5 V / 6 V devices), and three sub-cases a/b/c keyed on an N-well /
LVPWELL clearance (x or y): for LV the limit is 50 / 30 / 15 um, for MV
it is 15 um in every sub-case. The digital library here
(gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu9t5v0) is a 5 V library: every gate (Poly2 n Comp) in
the committed GDS lies inside DualGate (55/0), which the tool verifies
before it applies the MV column; if any gate were outside DualGate the
rule would be reported unsupported, because the LV limit depends on the
clearance x/y which this tool does not measure.
Distance definition used (the DRM says 'space ... to every point on the
boundary of'): for every point on the boundary of a 'subject' polygon,
the Euclidean distance to the nearest point of any qualifying 'tap'
polygon of the same well/substrate must not exceed the limit. Euclidean
(not Manhattan) is KLayout's own DRC 'space' default and is the smaller
of the two metrics, so a Manhattan reading could only fail more. The
tap polygon is the tap diffusion itself (distance is to its nearest
edge, not to a contact or its centre).
Layer algebra, taken from the PDK's own main.drc:
ncomp = Comp & Nplus        pcomp = Comp & Pplus
ntap  = ncomp & Nwell       ptap  = pcomp - Nwell
Rules checked:
- LU.4 (no DNWELL): subject = pcomp & Nwell (PCOMP inside Nwell);
tap = ntap, in the SAME Nwell island as the subject point (a tap in a
different, merely nearby well does not tie this well).
- LU.3 (no DNWELL): subject = ncomp - Nwell (NCOMP outside Nwell); tap =
ptap (Psub/LVPWELL tap outside Nwell). The substrate is one body, so
there is no island restriction.
Electrical identity (DRM guidelines LU.9 / LU.10: Nwell taps to the most
positive potential, Psub taps to the most negative): a tap only counts
toward LU.3/LU.4 if its extracted net carries a supply name for the
required rail (ntap -> VDD side, ptap -> VSS side). Connectivity is
extracted from the stream (tap diffusion -> Contact -> Metal1 -> Via1 ->
... -> Metal5, with 34/10 and 81/10 text as net names). A nearby tap on
the wrong rail, or on a net that carries neither rail name, is reported
and EXCLUDED from coverage. Reporting also records the geometry-only
worst distance so the effect of the exclusion is visible.
Not checked, and reported as not_applicable (provably absent geometry)
or unsupported (never as pass): LU.1 / LU.2 (apply inside DNWELL; the
stream has no DNWELL 12/0 -- verified, else unsupported), LU.5 (NAT 5/0
present only; verified absent), LU.7 / LU.8 (guidelines), LU.9 / LU.10
(guidelines; identity above is an input to LU.3/LU.4, not a proof of
potential ordering), and DRM 14.3.2 (I/O latch-up; needs the
Latchup_MK 137/5 marker semantics the tool does not evaluate).
The OpenROAD `tapcell -distance 100` configured in build.py is a
placement parameter. It is not used or trusted here; only the committed
stream's geometry is measured.

rules.description: Max Nwell tap space to every point on the boundary of PCOMP inside Nwell (outside DNWELL)
rules.subject: pcomp_in_nwell

rules.description: Max Psub (LVPWELL) tap space to every point on the boundary of NCOMP outside Nwell (outside DNWELL)
rules.subject: ncomp_outside_nwell

rules.description: Max Nwell/DNWELL tap space for PCOMP inside DNWELL
Max LVPWELL tap space for NCOMP inside LVPWELL within DNWELL
Native-Vt NMOS (NAT) must be surrounded by a PCOMP guard ring

rules.reason: Guideline (contact count / 3% equivalent contact area); not coded by the DRM (Appendix B) and not measured here.
Guideline (butted substrate contact to source); not coded by the DRM and not measured here.
Guideline (Nwell taps at the highest potential). Rail identity is used as an input to LU.3/LU.4, but potential ordering is not proven.
Guideline (Psub at the lowest potential). Rail identity is used as an input to LU.3/LU.4, but potential ordering is not proven.
I/O latch-up rules (Latchup_MK-marked diffusions) are not evaluated by this tool.
